title: Assignment 7: E-Waste Awareness Campaign
summary: Spearheaded the campus E-Waste Awareness Campaign as the official Myth Buster Quiz Host — actively educating and engaging participants through live myth-busting sessions and an original 5-part research-backed visual poster series addressing common misconceptions about electronics disposal.

posters.title: Tiny Gadgets
posters.myth: A single wireless earbud is too small to count as e-waste.
posters.truth: Small Device. Big Impact. Contains critical lithium, cobalt, and toxic components.

posters.title: Gold in Phones
posters.myth: Every old smartphone contains enough gold to buy a new smartphone.
posters.truth: Precious Materials Deserve a Second Life — only trace amounts, viable at industrial scale.

posters.title: Working Electronics
posters.myth: A device cannot be e-waste if it still switches on.
posters.truth: Working Doesn't Mean Worthless — repair, refurbish, or recycle responsibly.

posters.title: Perfect Recycling
posters.myth: Recycling centres recover 100% of every electronic device.
posters.truth: Recycling Isn't Perfect — But It Matters. Proper e-waste facilities maximize recovery.

posters.title: Old Chargers
posters.myth: Old chargers are just cables, so they aren't e-waste.
posters.truth: A Charger Is Electronics Too — packed with circuit boards and recoverable copper.
